subject: Bryton: post-demo integration checklist & repro plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Palmer <apalmer@bryton.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bryton: post-demo integration checklist & repro plan

Hi Alex —

Great talking today. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we’re aligned:

- Goal: get a minimal sandbox integration working (text generation + embeddings for search rerank) by EOD next Tuesday.
- Priority blockers you called out: auth failures during SDK handshake and intermittent 502s on multi-part payloads.
- Owners: Neha (product/sales), Marissa (solutions), Jordan (integration/SDK), Priyom (support/triage).

Action items:
1) Bryton: push a representative test payload (same as you used in demo) to our sandbox URL and send the log capture (you mentioned you have a capture).
2) Redwood: we’ll share a short repro playbook and a sample curl + SDK snippet you can run locally.
3) If 502s persist, Jordan/Priyom will provide a targeted capture command and a temporary config patch to increase request timeouts and disable auto-batching for the route.

Attachments: integration-checklist.xlsx (checklist + minimal payload), sample curl in body below.

Sample curl (sandbox):
curl -X POST https://sandbox.api.redwood.com/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ME" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-1.0","input":"Summarize customer invoice lines","max_tokens":150}'

If you can run that and paste the full response + the 502 capture, we’ll start the repro run immediately. Can we do a 30-min triage call Thursday 10am PT if needed?

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Palmer <apalmer@bryton.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Bryton Procurement <procurement@bryton.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bryton: post-demo integration checklist & repro plan

Neha — thanks for the clear next steps. Quick update from our side: we ran the curl you provided against the sandbox and got a 502 on ~30% of requests when payloads include an "embeddings" block along with the generation request (we're doing a combined call to save round trips). Attached is the raw tcpdump we captured plus the 502 response body (see capture-502-log.txt).

Additionally: our dev noticed an intermittent auth error when using the official Node SDK — the token is valid and not expired, but calls fail with "invalid_token" on the first attempt and succeed if retried. We can reproduce this reliably in our CI job ~1/10 runs.

We’d like the playbook and any temporary config suggestions. If you can include a minimal SDK example that mirrors our combined payload shape, that would help.

Alex
Alex Palmer
Head of Integrations, Bryton AI

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Palmer <apalmer@bryton.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 12:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bryton: post-demo integration checklist & repro plan

Thanks Alex — attaching the checklist and an initial repro playbook. Looping in Jordan and Priyom to triage the two failure modes (502 with combined payload, & intermittent SDK auth).

Jordan/Priyom: quick context from Bryton: they bundle an embeddings call + generation in one POST to reduce latency. Payload shape attached in the checklist (see sheet "combined-payload"). They see 502s when embedding size > ~2k tokens and the route is being autoprocessed by our batching layer. Also they report SDK invalid_token on first trial in CI (token is the same across retries).

Preliminary repro steps we’ll try (Priyom / Jordan to confirm):
- Step 1: run the attached tcpdump through our capture parser to surface the exact request body and headers (they attached capture-502-log.txt).
- Step 2: reproduce locally with the sample curl + an explicit header: X-Disable-Batching: true (this will bypass continuous batching for that route). If 502 disappears, that points to a batching edge case with combined payloads.
- Step 3: for the SDK invalid_token: Jordan to provide an instrumented Node snippet with debug logging of the auth refresh lifecycle; Priyom to validate whether our token validation/clock skew checks might intermittently fail under short-lived CI runners.

Temporary mitigations to try now:
- For Bryton CI: set SDK option retryOnAuthError: true and increase token refresh window to 60s (we’ll provide patch).
- For Sandbox: disable auto-batching on the route for 24-48h while we triage.

I’ve attached sdk-config.patch with the small client-side change to enable retryOnAuthError and a recommended timeout bump.

If you can confirm a good time for the triage call (Thursday 10am PT still good?) we’ll schedule and share a short runbook beforehand.

-Neha

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Palmer <apalmer@bryton.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bryton: post-demo integration checklist & repro plan

Alex / team — I started a repro on a local branch. Quick notes and the commands I used so you can reproduce exactly:

- Environment: node v18.16, redwood-js-sdk@2.3.1 (with our patch applied), macOS Monterey.
- Repro command (curl mirror):
  curl -X POST https://sandbox.api.redwood.com/v1/combined 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -H "X-Disable-Batching: true" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-1.0","generation":{"input":"Summarize lines"},"embeddings":{"input":["full invoice text repeated to ~2200 tokens"]}}'

Results: with X-Disable-Batching: true, I cannot reproduce 502s locally. With batching enabled, I see a consistent 502 once the embeddings block > ~1800 tokens and when the batcher attempts to coalesce multiple small generation requests (likely an alignment bug in the batching assembler).

Log excerpt I captured (attached as capture-502-log.txt):
- upstream/generator | request_length=24321 | kernel_select=matmul-fuse-v2 | batch_coalesced=3
- runtime/error | code=E5XX_INTERNAL | msg="tensor layout mismatch during fused attention multiply"

Suggested short-term fixes:
1) Sandbox config: keep X-Disable-Batching for Bryton route for 48 hours (Neha can flip).
2) Batching assembler: add a safety guard to avoid fusing embeddings + generation when embeddings.token_count > 1600. I’ll open a PR with the guard and a unit test.
3) SDK: the invalid_token behavior looks like a clock-skew edge case during token refresh in our Node client when the system clock jumps (common in ephemeral CI containers). Jordan and I recommend enabling retryOnAuthError: true and adding a 2s jitter to refresh scheduling. Attached sdk-config.patch (small client middleware) — apply to your SDK before running CI.

I’ll open PRs and paste links into the shared drive folder. If you want, we can try these changes in a canary sandbox this afternoon.

-Priyom

From: Alex Palmer <apalmer@bryton.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Bryton Procurement <procurement@bryton.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bryton: post-demo integration checklist & repro plan

Neha/Priyom/Jordan — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the clear repro steps. We ran the curl with X-Disable-Batching: true and confirmed the 502s disappear. We also applied the sdk-config.patch in our CI sandbox and the invalid_token error rate dropped to 0/50 runs.

Next steps per Bryton:
- We’ll leave batching disabled for the route in sandbox for 48 hours while you push the batching fix.
- Please share the PRs and a quick summary of the guard you’re adding (test plan + rollback).
- We’ll prep a short procurement note (cc'ed) asking for a pilot order once we validate end-to-end in the next week.

Confirming Thursday 10am PT is still useful; we’ll take that slot for a 30-min sync to review PRs and canary results.

Appreciate the help — Alex
